findings.text: This family is relational and covenantal, not individual-moral: its dominant shape is betrayal of a bond, and the same vocabulary serves, without distinction, a betrayed human relationship and a betrayed covenant with God. H0898 (bagad, 28 verses) runs both registers in the same small set of texts: even your brothers have dealt treacherously with you (Jer 12:6, a family betrayal) sits alongside the treacherous sister Judah set against faithless Israel (Jer 3:8, 3:11, the marriage-infidelity figure for covenant breach).
Proverbs uses H0898 structurally, as a fixed class opposed to the upright, destroyed by their own conduct (Prov 11:3, 11:6, 13:15).

H4603/H4604 (ma'al, 30 verses combined) is the most explicit: its meaning block splits the root directly into against man and against God senses, and the verses bear this out one for one: Achan's sacrilege against devoted objects (Josh 7:1), a wife's suspected unfaithfulness under the jealousy ordeal (Num 5:27), and national apostasy and idolatry (2 Chr 26:16, 28:19, Ezek 14:13, 15:8, 17:20, 39:26) sit in the same lexical family as ordinary interpersonal deception (Lev 6:2, deceiving his neighbor).
findings.flag: Ezek 14:13, 15:8, 17:20 and 39:26 are given without the book name and are not resolved by the index

findings.text: The ma'al term also feeds directly into the guilt-offering system (Lev 5:15, 6:2), the same institution documented in the guilt subgroup (#1680 v2): a ma'al-breach is precisely the kind of unfaithfulness the asham (guilt offering) exists to remedy.

G0646, G0763 and G0764 (Greek) shift register slightly: less about a specific broken bond, more a general orientation of impiety opposed to godliness as a category (Rom 1:18 pairs ungodliness with unrighteousness; Titus 2:12 opposes it to living self-controlled, upright and godly).
G0646 (apostasia) names departure from a founding standard (forsaking Mosaic custom, Acts 21:21; the eschatological rebellion, 2 Thess 2:3) rather than a relational breach as such.

H5627 (sarah) adds a distinct instigation sense: it names speaking rebellion, inciting others toward covenant abandonment (Deut 13:5's false prophet who taught rebellion; Jer 28:16, 29:32, prophets who uttered or spoke rebellion against the LORD), a verbal-agency variant not present in the other members.
findings.flag: Jer 29:32 is given without the book name and is not resolved by the index

findings.text: The marriage-infidelity-for-covenant-breach structure this family shows in H0898 and H4603 is the same structure driving the C (adultery and sexual sin) family's Hosea, Jeremiah and Ezekiel 23 material: both families independently land on the same metaphor. Treated as separate gloss-families, C and J partly describe one and the same underlying figure from two lexical angles (adultery-vocabulary and treachery-vocabulary), a case where the gloss-text grouping method splits what the verses themselves treat as one figure.
